overlap_analysis.finding: The three files are one arc: lecture03 creates the schema, lecture04 writes and changes data in it, lecture05 reads it back. Splitting them would strand DML statements from the constraints that reject them, so they are batched together at 183 prose lines — half the B4 ceiling.
overlap_analysis.disposition: Where the lectures re-teach something the db.* namespace already holds, the evidence is appended to the applied concept rather than duplicated: SQL itself, and the primary, unique and foreign keys that lecture02 introduced as model concepts and lecture03 now shows as DDL. Three new subdomains open: db.sql for the language surface, db.type for the attribute data types, db.index for the one place the course names an index.

candidates.title: SQL
candidates.concept_granularity: single language in which today's systems merge what were once three - definition, view and manipulation - the relational database language being SQL

candidates.title: 기본키
candidates.concept_granularity: single candidate key chosen to identify tuples, usually the one with fewest attributes, conventionally marked by underlining

candidates.title: 유일키
candidates.concept_granularity: single candidate key that was not chosen as the primary one

candidates.title: 외래키
candidates.concept_granularity: single attribute set referring to another relation's primary key

candidates.title: DB 스키마 정의 시 고려 요소
candidates.concept_granularity: single judgment made before any DDL is written: the schema must be settled against the service spec, data consistency, convenience and extensibility together, because it is what everything else is built on

candidates.title: 관계 모델과 SQL의 용어 대응
candidates.concept_granularity: single table of correspondences between the relational data model's vocabulary and SQL's - relation becomes table, attribute becomes column, tuple becomes row, and domain keeps its name

candidates.title: SQL에서의 relation은 multiset
candidates.concept_granularity: single divergence between theory and SQL: the relational model defines a relation as a set so no tuple may repeat, but SQL defines it as a multiset (bag) so duplicate tuples are allowed

candidates.title: 데이터베이스 기본 명령어
candidates.concept_granularity: single set of statements that operate on databases rather than on data - listing them, creating one, asking which one is currently selected, selecting one, and dropping one

candidates.title: DATABASE와 SCHEMA의 관계
candidates.concept_granularity: single ambiguity in the word schema across products: MySQL treats DATABASE and SCHEMA as the same thing, while PostgreSQL makes SCHEMA a namespace inside a DATABASE so one database holds many schemas and each schema holds tables

candidates.title: 정수 타입의 RDBMS별 차이
candidates.concept_granularity: single caveat that the integer type family is not the same everywhere - PostgreSQL offers only SMALLINT, INT/INTEGER and BIGINT, with no TINYINT or MEDIUMINT

candidates.title: 고정 소수점 타입
candidates.concept_granularity: single fixed-point type declared as DECIMAL(precision, scale) where precision is the digit count and scale the digits after the point, and whose overflow handling differs - the SQL standard makes DECIMAL lenient and NUMERIC strict, while MySQL treats both strictly and truncates to the declared precision

candidates.title: CHAR와 VARCHAR
candidates.concept_granularity: single choice between the fixed-length and variable-length string types, which cannot be settled in the abstract because each RDBMS implements them differently - PostgreSQL recommends VARCHAR outright, while in MySQL VARCHAR saves storage but can cost time, so a fixed-width attribute like a form number is better as CHAR

candidates.title: TEXT 계열 타입
candidates.concept_granularity: single family of long string types whose membership is product-specific - PostgreSQL has only TEXT, MySQL splits it into four where MEDIUMTEXT and LONGTEXT hold more than VARCHAR and TINYTEXT and TEXT hold the same or less

candidates.title: 날짜와 시간 타입
candidates.concept_granularity: single distinction between DATETIME and TIMESTAMP - they differ in range and in time-zone handling, because MySQL converts a TIMESTAMP from the server's or its own configured zone into UTC on write and converts it back on read, so TIMESTAMP is affected by time-zone and DATETIME is not

candidates.title: boolean 타입의 부재
candidates.concept_granularity: single gap in MySQL's type list - it has no boolean type, so a truth value is stored as TINYINT holding 0 or 1, whereas PostgreSQL provides one

candidates.title: 속성 DEFAULT
candidates.concept_granularity: single value declared for an attribute that is stored in its place when a new tuple arrives without one

candidates.title: ALTER TABLE
candidates.concept_granularity: single statement that changes an existing table's schema, and the operational caution that comes with it - if the table is already in service, the change must be reviewed for its effect on the backend before it is run

candidates.title: DROP TABLE
candidates.concept_granularity: single statement that removes a table

candidates.title: NOT NULL 제약조건
candidates.concept_granularity: single constraint forbidding NULL as a value for an attribute, usually declared together with UNIQUE because UNIQUE alone may still let NULL repeat

candidates.title: CHECK 제약조건
candidates.concept_granularity: single constraint restricting which values an attribute may hold, so an INSERT carrying a value outside the declared range is rejected

candidates.title: 참조 무결성 옵션
candidates.concept_granularity: single option attached to a FOREIGN KEY that decides what happens to the referencing value when the referenced one is deleted or updated - CASCADE follows it, SET NULL blanks it, RESTRICT refuses the change, NO ACTION defers the check to the end of the transaction, and SET DEFAULT falls back to the default, with MySQL supporting only the first three in practice

candidates.title: 제약조건 이름 명시
candidates.concept_granularity: single habit of naming a constraint when declaring it, which makes a violation message say which constraint was broken and lets the constraint be dropped by that name later

candidates.title: 실습용 회사 스키마
candidates.concept_granularity: single worked example carried through the rest of the course - an IT company relational database over departments, employees and projects on MySQL InnoDB, written from a data model into a schema, where DEPARTMENT's leader_id could not be a FOREIGN KEY at creation time because EMPLOYEE did not exist yet and had to be added afterwards

candidates.title: INSERT
candidates.concept_granularity: single statement adding tuples to a table in three forms - values only, which must follow the declared attribute order and fill every attribute; attribute names with values, which frees the order and lets omitted attributes fall back to DEFAULT or NULL; and several value lists at once for many tuples in one statement

candidates.title: UPDATE
candidates.concept_granularity: single statement changing attribute values in the tuples a WHERE clause selects, which may span two tables by naming both in the statement and joining them in the condition, and which is best written as table.attribute so the reader can tell where each name comes from

candidates.title: DELETE
candidates.concept_granularity: single statement removing the tuples a WHERE clause selects, which erases every tuple in the table when that clause is left out, and whose condition may exclude rather than match using <> (equivalently !=)

candidates.title: 제약조건 위반 에러
candidates.concept_granularity: single way constraints make themselves felt at INSERT time - a duplicate primary key, a value outside a CHECK range, and a foreign key whose referenced value does not actually exist in the other table each fail the statement, with SHOW CREATE TABLE available to see which constraints the table carries

candidates.title: SELECT
candidates.concept_granularity: single statement reading tuples out of a table, made of two parts worth naming separately - the selection condition in WHERE that decides which tuples, and the projection condition in the attribute list that decides which attributes

candidates.title: join condition
candidates.concept_granularity: single third kind of condition beside selection and projection - the one linking two tables by equating a column of each, which forces every ambiguous name in the statement to be qualified with its table or the query fails as ambiguous

candidates.title: AS 별칭
candidates.concept_granularity: single keyword giving a table or an attribute another name, which is what lets a result column say whose id it is rather than just id, and which may be omitted entirely

candidates.title: DISTINCT
candidates.concept_granularity: single keyword dropping duplicate tuples from a SELECT result, which is needed precisely because a join can produce the same row more than once and SQL does not remove it on its own

candidates.title: LIKE
candidates.concept_granularity: single operator matching a string against a pattern, where % stands for any number of characters and _ for exactly one, and where a literal % or _ must be escaped with a backslash to be searched for

candidates.title: asterisk
candidates.concept_granularity: single shorthand standing for every attribute of the selected tuples

candidates.title: 조회 조건과 인덱스
candidates.concept_granularity: single rule for writing queries that keep working as data grows - the attributes named in the conditions must have an index, or the query slows down in proportion to the table's size
